lane: WBG4-SSCC (strike-conditioned structural corridor), blind feature set
hypothesis: A supervised detector fitted on public USGS-derived layers only — lidar scarp morphology, GeoDAWN radiometrics and their ratio/upward-continuation extensions, SGMC fault geometry, GDR-1391 spring density — recovers withheld whole fault components better than a structure-only dot prior does, and therefore has a better chance of firing on faults that are absent from the catalogues.
mechanism: Multi-scale scarp/curvature relief with strike continuity, radiometric contrast and independent structural context; per-pixel probabilities from gradient-boosted trees; emitted set = top-k model scores at the operating point that maximises pooled holdout DTI.
non_fault_mimic: Bedrock ridge crests, landslide head scarps and fluvial terrace edges produce the same short-wavelength coherent relief; alluvial-fan and playa boundaries produce radiometric contrast without faulting.

holdout.evaluator: wbg4-hide-recover-v1 (whole components, 3 px buffer, 2x2 quadrants, visible-only catalogue features, exact visible mask, rank-cut operating point)
holdout.ci95_method: 4 spatial quadrant blocks resampled with replacement, 256 resamples; coarse by construction
holdout.note: Holdout target is withheld CATALOGUE faults, not the experts' new faults; the registry comparison below shows this metric does not predict leaderboard score (LOO R2 < 0).

negative_result.interpretation: 'Be near the mapped catalogue' is not a fault detector under hide-and-recover: it re-detects the faults that were not withheld and earns no credit for the withheld ones.

uniqueness.literal_3px_rule: unsatisfiable: the GEMSDOE13 stride-5 lattice gives the organizer-accepted files 99.91-99.92 % overlap and this file 99.84 %
uniqueness.verdict: not a copy; method is new and rank correlation passes everywhere

registry_calibration.conclusion: no defensible leaderboard point estimate for this file
